subject: pharmacology
title: Biologic Controllers, Targeted PDE4 Inhibitors, and Centrally Acting Antitussives

steps.tx: The recombinant humanized IgG1-kappa monoclonal antibody that binds selectively to the constant Fc region of free human immunoglobulin E is **omalizumab**. By binding only to free circulating IgE and not to IgE already bound to high-affinity Fc-epsilon-RI receptors on mast cells and basophils, omalizumab prevents antigen-induced cross-linking and subsequent degranulation without triggering anaphylaxis itself. In addition, it downregulates Fc-epsilon-RI receptor expression on basophils and dendritic cells over several months, indicated for moderate-to-severe allergic asthma with elevated baseline serum IgE.
steps.say: Omalizumab neutralizes free circulating IgE to prevent mast cell degranulation and downregulate surface IgE receptors.

steps.tx: A humanized monoclonal antibody directed specifically against human interleukin-5 that halts eosinophil maturation and recruitment is **mepolizumab**. Administered subcutaneously once every four weeks at 100 mg, mepolizumab neutralizes circulating interleukin-5, depriving eosinophils of their primary survival, differentiation, and trafficking cytokine. This results in profound and sustained reductions in blood and tissue eosinophil counts, dramatically reducing asthma exacerbation rates, emergency department visits, and maintenance oral corticosteroid requirements in patients with severe refractory eosinophilic asthma phenotype.
steps.say: Mepolizumab neutralizes interleukin-5 to deplete eosinophils and reduce severe asthma exacerbations.

left.title: Anti-IL-5 Ligand Antibody (Mepolizumab)
points: Binds and neutralizes circulating interleukin-5 cytokine directly
Deprives eosinophils of survival and bone marrow maturation signal
Administered as 100 mg subcutaneous injection every 4 weeks
Substantially reduces oral corticosteroid maintenance burden

right.title: Anti-IL-5 Receptor Antibody (Benralizumab)
points: Binds specifically to the IL-5R-alpha receptor on eosinophils
Afucosylated Fc domain recruits NK cells for ADCC lysis
Produces near-complete depletion of circulating eosinophils in 24 hours
Administered subcutaneously every 8 weeks following induction

steps.tx: The orally active, selective non-xanthine phosphodiesterase-4 inhibitor approved specifically for maintenance therapy in severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is **roflumilast**. Because PDE4 is the predominant cyclic AMP-metabolizing enzyme in inflammatory leukocytes, roflumilast elevates intracellular cyclic AMP, suppressing leukocyte activation, chemotaxis, and release of pro-inflammatory mediators. Indicated for severe COPD associated with chronic bronchitis and frequent exacerbations, its common adverse effects include nausea, diarrhea, decreased appetite, and significant weight loss, alongside rare psychiatric disturbances like anxiety and depression.
steps.say: Roflumilast selectively inhibits PDE4 to suppress leukocyte inflammation and exacerbations in severe chronic bronchitis COPD.

steps.tx: The prototypical natural phenanthrene opioid alkaloid that functions as an effective centrally acting antitussive is **codeine** (methylmorphine). Ingested orally in antitussive doses of 10 to 20 mg, codeine penetrates the central nervous system to stimulate mu-opioid receptors within the medullary cough center, raising the threshold for cough reflex initiation. While highly effective for exhausting dry, non-productive nocturnal cough, codeine produces dose-dependent sedation, constipation, nausea, respiratory depression, and potential abuse liability, and is bioactivated to morphine via polymorphic CYP2D6 enzymes.
steps.say: Codeine suppresses the medullary cough center via mu-opioid receptors, but causes constipation and sedation.

left.title: Opioid Antitussive (Codeine)
points: Stimulates central medullary mu-opioid receptors directly
Produces significant sedation, respiratory depression, constipation
Bioactivated to morphine via polymorphic hepatic CYP2D6
Carries definite abuse potential and physical dependence risk

right.title: Non-Opioid Antitussive (Dextromethorphan)
points: Blocks NMDA receptors and stimulates sigma-1 receptors
Negligible sedation, zero respiratory depression or constipation
Lacks analgesic activity or classical opioid receptor binding
Minimal abuse liability at standard recommended oral doses

steps.tx: The synthetic d-isomer of the codeine analogue levorphanol that provides potent centrally acting antitussive efficacy without opioid analgesia or respiratory depression is **dextromethorphan**. Acting as an antagonist at N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors and an agonist at sigma-1 receptors within the brainstem medullary cough center, dextromethorphan elevates the sensory cough threshold equivalent to codeine. Because it lacks affinity for classical mu or kappa opioid receptors, it does not cause constipation, respiratory suppression, or physical dependence at therapeutic doses, making it the preferred non-narcotic cough suppressant.
steps.say: Dextromethorphan acts on NMDA and sigma-1 receptors to suppress dry cough without opioid bowel or respiratory risks.

nodes.label: Crosses blood-brain barrier into brainstem medullary nuclei
Sigma-1 receptor agonism and NMDA receptor antagonism
Elevation of sensory cough threshold and cessation of dry hacking cough

steps.tx: A unique peripherally acting non-opioid antitussive chemically related to the local anesthetic tetracaine is **benzonatate**. Ingested as liquid-filled gelatin perles, benzonatate acts locally in the respiratory tract by anesthetizing stretch receptors located within the vagal sensory afferents of the bronchial tree, lungs, and pleura. This dampens the afferent limb of the cough reflex triggered by deep breathing or mucosal irritation. The capsules must be swallowed whole without chewing; biting or crushing the perles causes rapid oral and oropharyngeal anesthesia, choking, and rare laryngospasm.
steps.say: Benzonatate anesthetizes airway stretch receptors peripherally, but chewing the capsule risks dangerous oropharyngeal numbness.

left.title: Peripherally Acting Antitussive (Benzonatate)
points: Chemically related to ester local anesthetic tetracaine
Anesthetizes stretch receptors on vagal pulmonary afferents
Zero central nervous system or medullary cough suppression
Must be swallowed whole; chewing triggers oropharyngeal choking

right.title: Centrally Acting Antitussives (Codeine, Dextromethorphan)
points: Cross blood-brain barrier into dorsal brainstem nuclei
Raise threshold of central medullary cough coordination center
Effective regardless of whether stimulus is peripheral or central
Available as oral liquids, syrups, and conventional tablets

steps.tx: A humanized monoclonal antibody directed against the alpha subunit of the interleukin-5 receptor that induces direct eosinophil apoptosis is **benralizumab**. Engineered with an afucosylated Fc region that enhances binding affinity to Fc-gamma-RIIIa receptors on natural killer cells by over fifty-fold, benralizumab recruits natural killer cells to destroy eosinophils and basophils via antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. Administered subcutaneously every eight weeks following induction, it achieves complete depletion of blood eosinophils within twenty-four hours in severe eosinophilic asthma.
steps.say: Benralizumab recruits natural killer cells to destroy eosinophils via antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity.

nodes.label: High-affinity binding to IL-5R-alpha on eosinophils and basophils
Afucosylated Fc domain engages Fc-gamma-RIIIa on natural killer cells
Antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity: complete eosinophil apoptosis in 24 hours

steps.tx: A distinct clinical syndrome characterized by the classic Samter triad of bronchial asthma, recurrent nasal polyposis, and acute bronchospasm following cyclooxygenase-1 inhibition is **aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease** (AERD). In susceptible individuals, inhibition of COX-1 shunts arachidonic acid entirely into the 5-lipoxygenase pathway, while concurrently depleting protective prostaglandin E2, which normally restrains 5-lipoxygenase. This provokes massive, unregulated synthesis of cysteinyl leukotrienes, triggering violent bronchospasm, profuse rhinorrhea, conjunctival injection, and facial flushing within thirty to ninety minutes of NSAID ingestion.
steps.say: AERD shunts arachidonic acid to leukotrienes during COX-1 inhibition, triggering severe asthma flares and rhinorrhea.
